[Regarding how much one may litigate, and it contains one section]: Dayyanim do not sit in judgment over less than the value of a perutah, as it is not considered money regarding the return of theft or a lost object. Regarding a vessel worth less than the value of a perutah, it depends on a dispute that will be explained in siman 88. If they were required to sit regarding the value of a perutah, they complete the judgment even if the conclusion came to be over less than the value of a perutah, such as where the defendant admitted to half a perutah and returned it to the plaintiff, or the defendant emerged innocent in his judgment and turned and sued the plaintiff for half a perutah. And some say that even for the conclusion of the judgment they do not attend to less than the value of a perutah. And some have written that regarding an object that is present in specie, they attend to it even for less than the value of a perutah; and that which our sages, of blessed memory, said, "they do not attend to less than the value of a perutah," refers to a claim of money or an object that is not present in specie. If two partners sue one person for a perutah, even though for each of them it is half a perutah, nevertheless, since in the business of the partnership it is a perutah, they attend to it. But two who are not partners do not have the ability to sue for a perutah from one—half a perutah for this one and half a perutah for this one. If one sues two people for a perutah, they attend to it, since for the plaintiff it is money. And if a beit din attended to less than the value of a perutah, they have the status of a beit din regarding admission and being established as a liar [Netivot HaMishpat].
